entry.title: GFR 2017 — ULTRA MEMORY GUIDE: All Important Rule Numbers of Chapter 2 & 6 (Serial Order)
entry.official_text:
🗂️
Ultra Memory Guide · General Financial Rules, 2017
Complete Serial Rule Number Reference — Chapter 2 & Chapter 6
Every important rule, in order, with its one-line meaning. Memorise this table = Exam ready.
📘 Chapter 2: Rules 18 → 41 📗 Chapter 6A: Rules 143 → 176 (Goods) 📕 Chapter 6B: Rules 177 → 196 (Consulting) 📙 Chapter 6C: Rules 197 → 205 (Non-Consulting)
📘
GFR 2017 — Chapter 2
General System of Financial Management (Rules 18 to 41)
Rule No. Heading / Subject One-Line Meaning (Exam-Ready)
18 Remission of Revenue No revenue claim can be remitted or abandoned without the sanction of the competent authority.
19 Annual Revenue Remission Statement Departments submit an annual statement to the Audit & Accounts Officer on 1st of June. Individual remissions below ₹1,000 are excluded.
20 Power to make rules for Remission Departments may frame departmental rules for remission of revenue, subject to general rules issued by the Government.
21 Standards of Financial Propriety Every officer must ensure expenditure is not prima-facie more than the occasion demands — guided by the highest standards of propriety.
22 Expenditure from Public Funds No authority may incur any expenditure or enter into any liability involving expenditure from public funds without the sanction of the competent authority.
23 Delegation of Financial Powers Financial powers not delegated to subordinates vest exclusively in the Finance Ministry.
24 Consultation with Financial Adviser Before incurring any expenditure, Departments must consult their Financial Adviser.
25 Provision of Funds No expenditure shall be incurred from public revenues without provision of funds — must ensure budget exists before spending.
26 Responsibility of Controlling Officer The Controlling Officer is personally responsible for ensuring funds under his control are spent for the purposes they were granted and no excess occurs.
27 Control of Expenditure against Budget Ministries must maintain a monthly expenditure register and continuously monitor actuals vs. budget to prevent excess or surrender.
28 Previous Consent of Finance Ministry Prior Finance Ministry consent mandatory for granting land, assigning revenue, concession/lease of mineral/forest rights, water/power rights, or any relinquishment of revenue.
29 Communication of Sanctions to Audit All sanctions go to Audit — except 7 categories: Advances, Establishment (Appointment/Promotion/Transfer), Posts (Creation/Continuation/Abolition), Charge handover, GPF withdrawals, Contingency, and Routine sanctions.
30 Lapse of Sanctions Every sanction to expenditure automatically lapses if not acted upon within 12 months from the date of issue, unless otherwise specified.
31 Date of Effect of Sanction A sanction takes effect from the date of issue, unless a specific date is mentioned in the sanction order itself.
32 Remission of Disallowances & Write-off of Overpayments Disallowances by Audit on government servant payments can be remitted by competent authority. Overpayments may be written off if recovery is impractical.
33 Losses and Defalcations Any loss of public money/property must be reported to the next higher authority immediately. Petty losses up to ₹10,000 exempt. Losses exceeding ₹50,000 (fire/theft/fraud) → Police investigation mandatory.
34 Detailed Rules on Losses Every loss must be subjected to investigation both departmentally and through Police (where criminal activity is suspected).
35 Losses — Detailed Procedure Losses due to fire, theft, fraud or negligence must be reported to next higher authority with a preliminary report within 24 hours.
36 Report of Loss to Audit/Accounts Officer All losses exceeding ₹10,000 must be reported to the Principal Accounts Officer and the Audit Officer without delay.
37 Responsibility for Losses The Head of Office is personally responsible for any loss occurring due to fraud, negligence or any laxity in internal controls.
38 Prompt Disposal of Loss Cases All cases of losses must be investigated and finalized promptly — delays in write-off or recovery proceedings are not permitted.
39 Demand for Information by Audit Every officer must comply with any demand for records, information or explanations made by the Comptroller & Auditor General or Audit Officer.
40 Submission of Records to Audit All records, documents, books, accounts must be made available to Audit when required — failure to produce is a serious irregularity.
41 Handling of Secret/Top Secret Files by Audit Secret/Top Secret files must be sent personally to the Head of the Audit Office. They are NOT exempt from audit — only the delivery method is different.
📗
GFR 2017 — Chapter 6, Part A
Procurement of Goods (Rules 143 to 176)
Rule No. Heading / Subject One-Line Meaning (Exam-Ready)
143 Definition of Goods Goods = all tangible/intangible products including software, IP, services, transportation, installation, training. Excludes library books/periodicals.
144 Fundamental Principles of Procurement Description must be Objective, Functional, Generic, Measurable (O-F-G-M). Must NOT indicate a brand/trademark name.
145 Procurement for Defence/Security Procurement for defence mobilisation/security operations may be done under special powers delegated by the Government.
146 Powers of Procurement Delegated financial powers of Ministries/Departments for procurement of goods — head of department may further delegate subject to limits.
147 Purchase without Quotation Purchases up to ₹50,000 per occasion (for items not on GeM) can be made without any formal quotation.
148 Local Purchase Committee (LPC) For purchases ₹50,001 to ₹5,00,000 — a 3-member committee is constituted to handle local purchases.
149 Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE) For procurement up to ₹50 Lakhs. Tender sent directly to more than 3 eligible suppliers. No open advertisement needed.
150 Advertised Tender Enquiry (ATE) For procurement ₹50 Lakhs and above. Must be published openly. Minimum 3 weeks (4 weeks if foreign bidders) for submission.
151 Debarment from Bidding Corruption/BNS guilty → debarred up to 3 years. Code of Integrity breach → debarred up to 2 years.
152 Registration of Suppliers Suppliers may be registered by the Purchasing Department. Registration does not guarantee any order but facilitates participation in tenders.
153 Purchase Preference Policy Purchase preference to Central Public Sector Enterprises, Khadi/Village Industries, and MSEs as prescribed by Government orders.
154 Rate Contract (RC) & DGS&D Procurement of common-use goods through DGS&D Rate Contract or GeM — all Ministries must procure at the RC rate or below.
155 Two-Bid System For complex/technical goods — Technical & Financial bids submitted together in separate sealed envelopes. Technical opened first; Financial opened only for qualified bidders.
156 Single Tender Enquiry (STE) Buy from one source only if: (1) Sole manufacturer, (2) Emergency, or (3) Standardization requirement.
157 Contents of Bid/Tender Bid documents must contain complete specifications, evaluation criteria, terms, EMD requirements, delivery schedule, and penalty clauses.
158 Late Bids Bids received after the deadline shall NOT be considered — late bids must be returned unopened. No exceptions.
159 Mandatory E-Publishing (CPPP) All tender enquiries, corrigenda, and bid awards must be published on CPPP (eprocure.gov.in) — mandatory for all Ministries, departments, and autonomous bodies.
160 Mandatory E-Procurement All bids must be received electronically via NIC's portal or any other approved service provider. No offline/manual bid reception permitted.
161 Global Tender Enquiry (GTE) — Restriction No GTE permitted for procurements up to ₹200 Crores. GTE only allowed beyond ₹200 Cr with special approval.
162 Contents of Bidding Document The complete set of bidding documents should contain eligibility criteria, technical specs, evaluation methodology, contract terms, EMD/Performance Security details.
163 Maintenance Contract AMC/CMC contracts for equipment may be entered into only with the OEM or authorised service provider and on competitive basis.
164 Two-Stage Bidding For evolving requirements — Stage 1: technical bids only (no price). Stage 2: shortlisted bidders submit final bids with prices based on revised specs.
165 Receipt & Opening of Bids Bids must be opened publicly at the specified time/place in the presence of bidders or their authorised representatives.
166 Proprietary Article Certificate When procuring a proprietary article (one made by a single manufacturer), the competent authority must certify that the item is uniquely available from that source only.
167 Evaluation of Bids Bids must be evaluated based on pre-disclosed criteria only — no new criteria can be introduced post-tender. L1 (Lowest evaluated cost) principle applies.
168 Terms of Delivery Terms of delivery (FOR destination/ex-works) must be clearly stated in the tender. Default: FOR destination with transit insurance by supplier.
169 Negotiation with L1 Price negotiation is generally banned — only permitted in Single Tender (proprietary) or with prior approval of competent authority.
170 Award of Contract Contract awarded to the lowest evaluated responsive bidder (L1) who meets all qualification criteria. Award within bid validity period.
171 Integrity Pact For procurements above ₹5 Crore (as revised), an Integrity Pact must be signed between the buyer and bidders with an Independent External Monitor.
172 Buy-back Offer Old items may be offered for buy-back when procuring new similar goods — helps offset cost. Must be on "as-is-where-is" basis.
173 Energy Efficient Appliances (BEE) All electrical appliances procured must carry the notified threshold or higher BEE Star Rating. Lower-rated appliances cannot be procured.
174 Insurance of Goods All goods procured must be insured during transit, unless delivered FOR destination where supplier bears transit risk.
175 Bid Security (Earnest Money Deposit) 2% to 5% of estimated value. Valid for 45 days beyond bid validity. Refunded to unsuccessful bidders by the 30th day after contract award.
176 Performance Security 3% to 5% of contract value (revised w.e.f 01.01.2024). Valid for 60 days beyond completion of all obligations including warranty.
📕
GFR 2017 — Chapter 6, Part B
Procurement of Consulting Services (Rules 177 to 196)
Rule No. Heading / Subject One-Line Meaning (Exam-Ready)
177 Definition of Consulting Services Professional, intellectual, training & advisory services. Does NOT include direct engagement of retired Government servants.
178 Principles of Engaging Consultants Consultant selection must follow principles of economy, transparency, fairness, and quality — avoid conflict of interest.
179 Preparation of Terms of Reference TOR defines the scope, objectives, tasks, deliverables and timeline — must be precise and comprehensive before floating RFP.
180 Preparation of Cost Estimate A realistic cost estimate must be prepared before seeking proposals — helps determine the budget and evaluate financial bids.
181 Short-listing and Expression of Interest For complex assignments, a two-stage process: first invite EOI for short-listing, then send RFP to shortlisted firms only.
182 Preparation of Request for Proposal (RFP) The RFP must contain: Letter of Invitation, TOR, Evaluation Criteria, Contract Conditions — financial and technical proposals in separate sealed envelopes.
183 Quality & Cost Based Selection (QCBS) Final score = Technical (up to 80%) + Financial (min 20%). Default split: 70:30. Technical weightage must never exceed 80%.
184 Quality Based Selection (QBS) Selection based on technical quality alone — financial bid of the highest ranked technical proposal is then negotiated. Used for highly complex/specialised assignments.
185 Terms of Reference (TOR) TOR must contain 5 elements in order: Objective → Tasks → Timeline → Support → Deliverables (Mnemonic: O-T-T-S-D).
186 Fixed Budget Selection (FBS) Budget is disclosed upfront — consultant offering the best quality within the fixed budget is selected. Financial proposals exceeding budget are rejected.
187 Single Source Selection (SSS) Engagement of a consultant without competition — permitted only when: (a) a natural extension of prior work, (b) only one firm is qualified, or (c) emergency.
188 Selection of Individual Consultants Individual consultants may be hired for tasks where teams or institutional support are not required — selection based on qualifications and experience.
189 Procedure for Selection Published EOI → short-list → issue RFP → receive proposals → evaluate → negotiate → award. Minimum 3 shortlisted firms needed.
190 Contract Negotiations Negotiations only with the first-ranked proposer — cover TOR, methodology, staff, and financial terms. If unsuccessful, proceed to second-ranked.
191 Publication of Awards All consulting assignments awarded must be published on the CPPP portal for transparency.
192 Monitoring & Evaluation Ministry must monitor contract performance through periodic progress reports and evaluate deliverables against the TOR.
193 Least Cost System (LCS) Zero weightage for technical score after qualifying. The responsive, technically qualified proposal with the lowest evaluated cost wins.
194 Bid Security for Consulting EMD of 2% to 3% of estimated cost — exempt for MSEs and firms registered with appropriate authorities.
195 Performance Security for Consulting 5% to 10% of contract value — valid for 60 days beyond completion. Forfeited for non-performance or breach.
196 Payment Terms for Consulting Payment to consultants in milestones linked to deliverables. Advance payment (if any) not exceeding 10% of contract value against bank guarantee.
📙
GFR 2017 — Chapter 6, Part C
Procurement of Non-Consulting Services (Rules 197 to 205)
Rule No. Heading / Subject One-Line Meaning (Exam-Ready)
197 Definition of Non-Consulting Services Services with physical, measurable deliverables — security, maintenance, cleaning, vehicle hire, facilities management.
198 Powers for Procurement of Non-Consulting Services Financial powers for procurement of non-consulting services follow the same delegation as for Goods under Rule 146.
199 Modes of Procurement Procurement modes: Advertised Tender, Limited Tender, Single Tender — same as Goods procurement but adapted for service contracts.
200 Bid Document for Non-Consulting Services Bid documents must specify scope of work, service levels (SLAs), penalty clauses, and evaluation criteria clearly.
201 Bid Security for Non-Consulting Services EMD of 2% to 5% of estimated value, same as Goods procurement rules.
202 Performance Security for Non-Consulting 3% to 5% of contract value — valid until 60 days beyond completion of all contractual obligations.
203 Evaluation of Bids Non-consulting service bids evaluated on L1 basis (lowest cost) after meeting technical qualification criteria.
204 Contract Management Appointing authority must designate a Contract Management Officer to monitor service delivery and ensure compliance with SLAs.
205 Residual Provisions For any matter not specifically covered under Rules 197-204, the corresponding provisions for Goods procurement (Rules 143-176) shall apply.

🧠 The Master Memory System — Chapter 2 & Chapter 6 Clusters

Group rules into themes. Learn the theme → the numbers follow naturally.

📘 CHAPTER 2 — 9 Rules to Know (18 → 41)
18 · 19 💸 Revenue Rules — Remission & Annual June Statement. Remember: "18-19 = Two rules for Revenue"
21 ⚖️ Propriety Rule — Rule 21 = 21-gun salute to good spending! "Don't spend more than needed."
23 · 24 📋 Delegation Duo — 23 = Powers vest in Finance Ministry if not delegated; 24 = Consult Financial Adviser. "23 and 24 work together like a door and its frame."
28 🔑 Consent Rule — 28 = "Wait 28 days... actually WAIT — ask Finance Ministry FIRST." Land, Revenue, Rights → prior consent needed.
29 📊 Audit Rule — 29 = "29 sanctions go to Audit... but not GPF, transfers, posts, advances!" The 7-exemption rule.
33 🚨 Losses Rule — Rule 33 = "33% of losses need police!" (losses >₹50K due to fraud/fire/theft). Petty losses ≤₹10K: no report needed.
41 🔒 Secret Rule — Rule 41 = "41 secrets go personally to the Audit Head." Not exempt — just delivered differently.
📗 CHAPTER 6A — GOODS RULES (143 → 176): The "Buying Ladder"
143 · 144 📖 Define & Guide — 143 = "What are Goods?" (143 items defined!). 144 = "Four Principles: O-F-G-M". They always come first.
147→150 🪜 The Buying Ladder (value increases with each rule):
147=No Quote(≤50K) → 148=LPC(50K-5L) → 149=LTE(≤50L) → 150=ATE(50L+)
151 🚫 Debarment — "151 = 1 rule, 5 letters (DEBAR), 1 decision." Corruption=3yr, Integrity=2yr.
155 · 156 📂 Bid Methods — 155 = Two-Bid (both submitted together); 156 = Single Tender (only 3 valid grounds). "155 splits; 156 singles."
159·160·161 🖥️ Digital Trio — "P-R-B": Publish(159=CPPP), Receive(160=NIC), Ban GTE(161=₹200Cr). Three consecutive rules, three digital mandates.
164 🔄 Two-Stage — "164 = 1 tender, 6 weeks apart, 4 shortlisted." Stage 1 = no price; Stage 2 = price. Used when specs are unclear.
166 📜 Proprietary Certificate — Rule 166 = one source, one certificate. Certify that only this manufacturer makes this product.
173 ⚡ BEE Star — "173 = 1 star minimum, 7 categories of appliances, 3-digit rule." Always buy the notified threshold or higher BEE Star Rating.
175 · 176 🔐 Security Pair — "B comes before P" → 175=Bid Security(2-5%, 45 days); 176=Performance Security(3-5%, 60 days). One letter apart; one rule apart.
📕 CHAPTER 6B — CONSULTING (177 → 193): The "D-S-T-C" Sequence
177 📖 Define — 177 = "1 definition, 7 types of consulting work." Intellectual, training, advisory. Not retired Govt. servants.
183 ⚖️ Score (QCBS) — 183 = "1 formula: 8 parts Technical, 3 parts Financial... wait, that's 80:30... no — 70:30 default, max 80% technical." Default always 70:30.
185 📝 Terms (TOR) — 185 = "1-8-5 = One Terms sheet with 5 elements: O·T·T·S·D" = Objective, Tasks, Timeline, Support, Deliverables.
193 💰 Cheapest (LCS) — 193 = "1 winner, 9 losers, 3 criteria to qualify... but only cost decides!" Zero weightage for tech after qualifying.
📙 CHAPTER 6C — NON-CONSULTING (197 → 205): "Physical Work Rules"
197 📦 Define — 197 = "1 definition, 9 types, 7 examples of physical work." Security, cleaning, maintenance, vehicle hire.
198–205 📋 Outsource — 8 rules (198 to 205) for hiring Non-Consulting services. Gap in rules? → Refer to Goods rules (135–176).

entry.title: GFR 2017: Financial Management, E-Procurement & Integrity — Rules 23, 24, 28, 29, 159, 160, 185 (Part 4 — Final)
entry.official_text:
📜
Ministry of Finance · General Financial Rules, 2017 — Part 4
Financial Powers, Prior Consents, E-Procurement & Integrity Framework

This final consolidation covers the governance layer of GFR 2017 — how financial powers flow, when the Finance Ministry must be consulted, and the mandatory digital infrastructure for public procurement.

⚖️
Rules 23 & 24
Delegation of Financial Powers
  • Financial powers of the Government that have not been delegated to a subordinate authority shall vest exclusively in the Finance Ministry.
  • Before incurring any expenditure, Departments and Ministries must consult with their Financial Adviser.
💡 Undelegated = Finance Ministry. Delegated = Subordinate authority. Pre-expenditure consultation with Financial Adviser is mandatory.
🔑
Rule 28
Previous Consent of Finance Ministry

Explicit prior consent from the Finance Ministry is required before any sanction involving:

Category What Requires Prior Finance Ministry Consent
🏞️ Land Grant of land by the Government
💰 Revenue Assignment of revenue or relinquishment of revenue in any way
🏗️ Concession Any concession, lease or licence of mineral or forest rights
💧 Resources Rights to water power or any other right of a similar nature
🔥 Exam Trigger: Any sanction that "gives away" a natural resource, land, or revenue right → Finance Ministry consent FIRST.
🖥️
Rules 159 & 160
Mandatory E-Publishing & E-Procurement
📢 Rule 159 — E-PUBLISHING 📩 Rule 160 — E-PROCUREMENT
All Ministries/Departments, attached/subordinate offices, and autonomous/statutory bodies must publish:
• Tender enquiries
• Corrigenda
• Details of bid awards

on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP). 		All Ministries/Departments must receive all bids electronically through e-procurement portals.

They may use:
• NIC's e-procurement solution, or
• Any other approved service provider following due process.

No offline / manual bid reception is permitted.
⚠️ Trap: Rule 159 = Publishing on CPPP (eprocure.gov.in). Rule 160 = Receiving bids via NIC or approved providers. Two separate mandates!
entry.guru_explanation:
🤝 Code of Integrity in Bidding — What Bidders Must Disclose

No official or bidder can accept bribes or unfair advantages. Bidders must compulsorily disclose at the time of bidding:

📋
Previous Transgressions
Any bribes, rule-breaking, or integrity violations committed in any country during the last 3 years.
🚫
Prior Debarments
If they have been debarred by any other procuring entity anywhere — this must be disclosed upfront.
⚡ Concealing past transgressions is itself a code of integrity violation — and can lead to debarment for up to 2 years.
🌐 Enlistment of Indian Agents for Foreign Principals

An Indian agent wanting to quote on behalf of a foreign company cannot simply submit a bid. They must follow a special process:

1️⃣
Mandatory Enlistment
Must enlist with GeM under the Compulsory Enlistment Scheme of the Dept. of Expenditure.
⚠️
Not Regular Registration
This enlistment is entirely different from normal supplier/vendor registration on GeM.
✅
Then Bid
Only after successful enlistment can the agent legally represent a foreign principal in any bid.
💡 This rule prevents foreign firms from circumventing Indian procurement norms by routing through unregistered local middlemen.
🧵 Reserved Items — Khadi & Handloom Textile Procurement
Textile Type Mandatory Quota Approved Sources
🧶 Khadi
Hand-spun & hand-woven textiles 		100%
Exclusively		 KVIC only — no other source permitted for Khadi procurement.
🪡 Handloom
General handloom origin textiles 		Min. 20%
of total		 KVIC, SHGs, cooperative societies, or weavers with a Pehchan card.
📋 Exceptions to Communication of Sanctions to Audit — Rule 29

Generally, all financial sanctions must be sent to the Audit/Accounts Officer. The following categories are explicitly exempt:

Category Sanction Type — Do NOT Endorse to Audit
Advances Grant of advances to Central Government employees
Establishment Appointment, promotion, or transfer of Gazetted and non-Gazetted Officers
Posts Creation, continuation, or abolition of posts
Charge Handing over and taking over of charge
Prov. Fund Payment or withdrawal of GPF advances to Government servants
Contingency Contingent expenditure sanctioned under powers of the Head of Office
Routine Issued by Heads of Subordinate Offices (other than proper Ministries/Departments)
📊 Key Numerical Limits at a Glance
Metric / Category Value / Limit
Global Tender Enquiry (GTE) — Prohibition Threshold No GTE up to ₹200 Crores
Mandatory Handloom Procurement (general textiles) At least 20%
Code of Integrity — Past Transgression Disclosure Window Last 3 years
Bid Security Validity (beyond bid validity period) 45 days
Budget Projection on GeM Portal Within 30 days of Budget approval
Refund of Unsuccessful Bidders' Bid Securities Latest by the 30th day after contract award
🏦 Conditions & Special Eligibility Rules
🖥️ E-Platform Flexibility
Ministries may use NIC's solution or any other approved service provider for e-procurement — they are not locked to one platform, provided due process is followed.
🔧 Non-Consulting Gap Rule
If a situation arises not covered under Non-Consulting Outsourcing rules (198–205), the department must refer to the Rules for Procurement of Goods (135–176) — NOT to consulting service rules.
📅 Budget Projection Obligation
All procuring requirements (whether on OPEX or CAPEX models) must be projected on the GeM portal within 30 days of the Budget being approved. This enables planning and transparency.
🔟 Terms of Reference (TOR) for Consultants — Rule 185

When hiring a consultant, the department must prepare a strict TOR containing all five elements in sequence:

1
Objective
Precise statement of objectives
2
Tasks
Outline of specific tasks to be carried out
3
Timeline
Fixed schedule for completion of tasks
4
Support
Inputs / support the Ministry will provide
5
Deliverables
Final outputs required of the Consultant
📌 Mnemonic: O T T S D → Objective · Tasks · Timeline · Support · Deliverables
entry.practical_example:
💰
Scenario 1 · Rule 29 — Audit Exemption
GPF Advance for Employee's Wedding — Does It Go to Audit?
📋 Situation
The Division Office sanctions a GPF advance for an employee's daughter's wedding. The Postmaster wonders whether to send a copy to the Audit Officer.
📜 The Rule
Under Rule 29, GPF withdrawals / advances to employees are explicitly in the exempt list — they are treated as routine personal finance actions, not public expenditure sanctions.
✅ Correct Action
The Postmaster does NOT need to endorse a copy to the Audit Officer. The sanction is complete without it.
💡 Other exempt cases: promotions, transfers, creation/abolition of posts, contingent expenditure by Head of Office.
🌐
Scenario 2 · Indian Agent for Foreign Principal
International Machinery Brand Bids via Delhi Representative
📋 Situation
An international machinery brand wants to bid for a high-value government contract through its local representative in Delhi.
🚫 What's NOT Allowed
The local representative cannot simply submit the bid as if they were a regular supplier — even if they are already registered on GeM as a vendor.
✅ Correct Action
They must first enlist under the Compulsory Enlistment Scheme for Indian Agents under the Dept. of Expenditure — a separate, mandatory process.
⚠️ Regular GeM vendor registration ≠ Enlistment as Indian Agent. Two completely different processes.

entry.title: GFR 2017: Revenue, Audits & Special Procurements — Rules 18, 19, 41, 173, 193 & Service Selection Methods
entry.official_text:
📜
Ministry of Finance · General Financial Rules, 2017
Revenue Remission, Audit Secrecy, Energy & Evaluation Rules

Part 3 covers rules that do not fit neatly into procurement alone — they govern how the Government handles revenue write-offs, secret documents during audits, energy standards, and the selection of the cheapest qualified service provider.

💸
Rules 18 & 19
Remission of Revenue
  • A claim to revenue shall not be remitted or abandoned save with the sanction of the competent authority.
  • Departments shall submit an Annual Statement on the 1st of June to the Audit and Accounts Officer.
  • However, individual remissions below ₹1,000 need not be included in this annual statement.
💡 Key Point: Even if a remission is below ₹1,000, it still requires competent authority sanction — it is just excluded from the annual reporting statement.
🔒
Rule 41
Handling of 'Secret' Files by Audit
Classification Required Procedure
🔴 Top Secret The file may be sent personally to the Head of the Audit Office, specifying the classification. The Head deals with it in accordance with standing instructions.
🟠 Secret Same procedure applies — sent personally to the Head of the Audit Office with the classification clearly specified.
⚠️ Critical: Secret/Top Secret files are NOT exempt from Audit. They are only handled via a special personal delivery channel.
⚡
Rule 173
Energy Efficient Appliances

Ministries/Departments, while procuring electrical appliances, shall ensure that they carry the notified threshold or higher Star Rating of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE). Procuring lower-rated appliances is not permitted.

📉
Rule 193
Least Cost System (LCS)
  • Under LCS, there is zero weightage for the technical score in the final evaluation.
  • The responsive, technically qualified proposal with the lowest evaluated cost is selected.
  • Technical evaluation is used only as a qualifying gate — not for scoring the final winner.
💡 LCS = Pass the technical test, then it's purely a price competition.
entry.guru_explanation:
👤 When to Use a Single Tender Enquiry (Nomination)

You can bypass competition and buy from a single source only under three specific circumstances:

🏭
Sole Manufacturer
It is in the absolute knowledge of the department that only one firm makes the product in question.
🚨
Emergency
A sudden, extreme emergency exists where delay caused by a tender process would be damaging.
🔩
Standardization
The item must be sourced from a specific firm to maintain standardization with existing equipment or systems.
🎨 Logo & Design Competitions — Transparent Selection

If a department needs a new logo or symbol, it cannot simply pick a designer at random. The rules require:

1. Public Competition:
A design competition must be held in a transparent manner with wide publicity.
2. CPPP Publication:
The competition must be posted on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) to ensure open access.
📋 Endorsing Sanctions — What Goes to Audit & What Does Not
✅ MUST BE SENT to Audit/Accounts Officer ❌ Do NOT Send (Routine Personal Sanctions)
All financial sanctions for expenditure, procurement, contracts, and non-routine approvals must go to the Audit/Accounts Officer. • GPF withdrawals granted to employees
• Grants of advances to employees
• Promotions and Transfers of staff
💡 Rule of Thumb: If it's about money leaving government coffers for services/goods, it goes to Audit. If it's a routine HR/personal finance action, it does not.
🗂️ Service Procurement Limits — Consulting vs. Non-Consulting
Service Type Estimated Value Procurement Method / Action Required
🤝 CONSULTING SERVICES (Intellectual / Advisory / Training)
Consulting Up to ₹50 Lakhs Prepare a long list of potential consultants via formal/informal enquiries. No need to publish EOI on CPPP.
Consulting Above ₹50 Lakhs Publish an 'Expression of Interest' (EOI) on CPPP to shortlist eligible consultants from the open market.
🔧 NON-CONSULTING SERVICES (Physical / Measurable Deliverables)
Non-Consulting Up to ₹50 Lakhs Issue a Limited Tender Enquiry to prima facie eligible contractors (minimum more than 3).
Non-Consulting Above ₹50 Lakhs Issue an advertisement on CPPP, GeM, and the organisation's own website for open competition.
📊 Key Numerical Limits at a Glance
Metric / Category Value / Limit
Annual Revenue Remission Statement — Exclusion Threshold Below ₹1,000
Advertised Tender Enquiry — Minimum Submission Time (Domestic) 3 weeks
Advertised Tender Enquiry — Minimum Submission Time (Foreign Bidders) 4 weeks
Minimum Shortlisted Consultants (for any selection method) Not less than 3
QCBS Technical Weightage — Maximum Permissible Must not exceed 80%
🏦 Rents, Fines & Special Conditions
🏢 Rents — Civil Departments
If a civil department (other than CPWD) maintains a rentable building, the Head of Department is responsible for recovering the rent from occupants.
⚖️ Fines — No Double Refund
Every authority imposing a fine must ensure it is deposited into the treasury without double refunds. Once paid, it cannot be refunded twice.
👤 Single Source Selection (Nomination) — For Consulting Services
Can only be used under exceptional circumstances: (1) Continuation of previous/related work, (2) Emergency or natural disaster, or (3) If only one consultant has the requisite expertise.
🔟 Consulting Services Bidding Process — Two-Bid System
  1. Submission: Consultants submit two separately sealed envelopes — a Technical Bid and a Financial Bid — placed inside one larger sealed outer envelope.
  2. First Opening: The purchasing department opens only the Technical Proposals on the specified date in the presence of the bidders' representatives.
  3. Technical Evaluation: The Consultancy Evaluation Committee (CEC) evaluates the technical bids and records reasons for acceptance and rejection of each.
  4. Second Opening: Financial bids of only the technically qualified bidders are opened for final evaluation and selection (via QCBS, LCS, or other applicable method).
💡 Financial bids of technically rejected consultants are never opened — they are returned unopened.
entry.practical_example:
💻
Scenario 1 · Single Tender Enquiry
Cyber-Attack Recovery — Only One Firm Makes the Required Software
📋 Situation
The Division Office suffers a cyber-attack and needs immediate recovery software that only one specific cybersecurity firm in India manufactures.
🔍 GFR Grounds
This satisfies Condition 1 for STE: it is in the absolute knowledge of the department that only a particular firm is the manufacturer.
✅ Correct Action
The department can proceed with a Single Tender Enquiry (STE) directly to that cybersecurity firm without inviting competitive bids.
⚠️ Even though it's an emergency, the STE is justified here primarily on grounds of sole manufacturer — both reasons independently qualify.
🧹
Scenario 2 · Non-Consulting Service Procurement
PMG Office — External Cleaning & Janitorial Service for ₹45 Lakhs
📋 Situation
PMG Office wants to hire an external cleaning and janitorial service for one year, estimated to cost ₹45 Lakhs.
🔍 Classification
Cleaning is a Non-Consulting Service (physical, measurable deliverables). At ₹45 Lakhs, it is within the ₹50 Lakh threshold.
✅ Correct Action
Issue a Limited Tender Enquiry to eligible contractors — must go to more than 3 of them. No CPPP advertisement needed.
💡 If the estimated cost were ₹55 Lakhs (above ₹50L), the office would need to advertise on CPPP, GeM, and its own website instead.

Fact / Common Trap ✅ Correct Answer

⚠️ "Secret/Top Secret files are exempt from audit scrutiny" FALSE. They are NOT exempt. They must be sent personally to the Head of the Audit Office.
📌 Annual Procurement Plans must be projected on GeM within 30 days of Budget approval

📌 Electrical appliances procured by Ministries must carry BEE Star Rating of the notified threshold or higher.
🧠 Key Distinctions — Compulsory for Exam
Concept A vs. Concept B

The technically qualified bidder with the lowest evaluated cost wins.
Used when technical quality is largely standard/routine. 		vs. QCBS — Quality & Cost Based
Technical score carries significant weight (default 70:30).
Final winner is the bidder with the highest combined score.
Used when expertise and quality of output truly matters.
ATE — Domestic Timeline
Minimum 3 weeks from publication date for bid submission. 		vs. ATE — Foreign Bidders Included
Minimum 4 weeks required to account for international logistics and communication.

₹1,000

3 firms

Replacing old items with newer versions

entry.title: GFR 2017: Procurement of Goods — Rules 142 to 176 (GeM, Tendering, Security & Bidding)
entry.official_text:
📜
Ministry of Finance · General Financial Rules, 2017
Legal Definitions & Authoritative Rules for Public Procurement of Goods

These provisions govern how Government Ministries and Departments must procure goods — covering everything from defining what "goods" are, to publishing tenders, to protecting the integrity of the bidding process.

📦
Rule 143
Definition of Goods
✅ INCLUDES ❌ STRICTLY EXCLUDES
• All tangible or intangible products
• Software, technology transfer
• Licenses, patents & intellectual properties
• Works and services
• Transportation, insurance
• Installation & commissioning
• Training and maintenance 		Books, publications, periodicals etc. procured for a library are strictly outside the definition of "Goods" under GFR Rule 143.
⚖️
Rule 144
Fundamental Principles of Public Procurement

The description of the subject matter of procurement must be:

🎯
Objective
Based on facts, not opinions
⚙️
Functional
Describes what it must do
🔤
Generic
No brand/trademark names
📏
Measurable
Quantifiable & verifiable
🚫 Must NOT indicate a requirement for a particular trade mark, trade name, or brand.
🖥️
Mandatory Requirement
Mandatory E-Publishing & E-Procurement
  • All Ministries/Departments must publish tender enquiries, corrigenda, and bid awards on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP).
  • It is mandatory to receive all bids through approved e-procurement portals (such as NIC or other approved providers).
💡 No manual / offline bid submission is allowed for procurements covered under e-procurement mandate.
🚫
Rule 151
Debarment from Bidding
Offence Debarment Period
Found guilty under Prevention of Corruption Act or BNS Up to 3 Years
Breaching the Code of Integrity Up to 2 Years
entry.guru_explanation:
🚫 The Rule Against Splitting — Anti-Fragmentation Principle

You cannot divide a demand for goods into smaller quantities just to make piecemeal purchases. This is strictly prohibited because it is a trick to:

❌ Trick 1: Avoid the mandatory L-1 bidding or GeM Reverse Auction by keeping value below the ₹10,00,000 threshold.
❌ Trick 2: Bypass the need for higher authority approval by splitting one big purchase into many small ones that fall under lower limits.
🧵 Textile Reservation Quotas — Protecting Local Weavers
Textile Type Mandatory Quota Source
Hand-spun & hand-woven textiles (Khadi) 100% exclusively KVIC only
General handloom origin textiles Minimum 20% SHGs, cooperative societies, or weavers with Pehchan card
🌐 Indian Agents & Foreign Principals — Enlistment Rule

If an Indian agent wants to submit a quote on behalf of a foreign company, they cannot just walk in and bid. They must:

1️⃣
Get Enlisted
Compulsorily enlist with GeM under the Dept. of Expenditure's scheme
⚠️
Special Process
This enlistment is completely different from normal supplier registration
✅
Then Bid
Only after enlistment can they legally represent a foreign principal
💰 Financial Limits for Procurement (Revised w.e.f. 10.07.2024)
Procurement Method Estimated Value Limit Condition / Action
🛒 GeM PROCUREMENT
GeM: Direct Purchase Up to ₹50,000 From any available supplier meeting quality/specs.
GeM: L-1 Bidding ₹50,001 to ₹10,00,000 Lowest price amongst at least 3 different manufacturers.
GeM: Online / Reverse Auction Above ₹10,00,000 Mandatory online bidding / reverse auction tools.
📋 NON-GeM / TENDER ENQUIRY (for items not available on GeM)
Without Quotation Up to ₹50,000 On each occasion, for items not on GeM.
Local Purchase Committee (LPC) ₹50,001 to ₹5,00,000 Constitution of a 3-member committee.
Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE) Up to ₹50 Lakhs Must invite more than 3 supplier firms.
Advertised Tender Enquiry (ATE) ₹50 Lakhs and above Minimum 3 weeks for submission (4 weeks if bids from abroad).
🔐 Security & Advance Payment Limits
Category Prescribed Limit Validity
Bid Security (Earnest Money) 2% to 5% of estimated value 45 days beyond final bid validity period
Performance Security 3% to 5% of contract value (revised w.e.f 01.01.2024) 60 days beyond completion of all obligations (incl. warranty)
Advance Payment (Private Firms) Max 30% of contract value —
Advance Payment (Govt / PSU) Max 40% of contract value —
Advance Payment (Maintenance Contracts) Max amount payable for 6 months —
🏦 Key Conditions & Eligibility
📅 Supplier Registration
Registered for a fixed period of 1 to 3 years. Must apply afresh for renewal after expiry.
✅ Bid Security Exemptions
Startups, MSMEs, GeM Registered Bidders, >₹500 Cr turnover (3 FYs), GeM Vendor Assessed, BIS Certified product suppliers.
👤 Single Tender (Nomination)
Allowed only if: (1) Only one firm makes the product, (2) Emergency situation, or (3) Standardization from a selected firm.
🚗 GeM Automobile Exemption
Automobiles procured through GeM are permitted as direct purchases up to L1 rules without any financial ceiling limit.
🔟 Two-Bid System vs. Two-Stage Bidding — Know the Difference
📂 TWO-BID SYSTEM
For complex / technical machinery		 🔄 TWO-STAGE BIDDING
For evolving requirements — Rule 164
  1. Submission: Technical and Financial bids received simultaneously — sealed in separate envelopes inside one outer envelope.
  2. Stage 1 Opening: Open and evaluate only the Technical bids first.
  3. Stage 2 Opening: Open Financial bids of only the technically qualified offers for final ranking and award.
  1. Stage 1: Invite bids via advertised tender containing only technical aspects — no bid price asked.
  2. Evaluation: Committee evaluates first-stage bids and refines the requirements.
  3. Stage 2: Invite all non-rejected bidders to submit a final bid with prices based on the revised specs.
💡 Use when specs are KNOWN but evaluation must be done in 2 phases 💡 Use when specs are NOT FULLY KNOWN and may evolve after seeing vendor capabilities
entry.practical_example:
⚙️
Scenario 1 · Two-Stage Bidding (Rule 164)
Procuring Sophisticated Sorting Machinery with Uncertain Specifications
📋 Situation
The Division Office needs highly sophisticated sorting machinery where the exact technical specifications might need adjustment after seeing what vendors can offer.
🔍 Why Two-Stage?
Specs are not fixed in advance. The department needs to learn from vendor proposals first, refine requirements, and then get final price bids on the improved specs.
✅ Correct Action
Use Two-Stage Bidding:
① Invite technical bids without prices
② Evaluate & refine specs
③ Ask shortlisted bidders for final price bids.
⚠️ Contrast: If specifications were already fully known, the Two-Bid System would be used instead — both envelopes submitted together.
⏰
Scenario 2 · Late Bid Rejection
Supplier Submits Bid Two Hours After the Official Deadline
📋 Situation
A supplier submits their bid for an Advertised Tender Enquiry two hours after the official deadline, claiming they were held up in traffic.
📜 The Rule
For Advertised or Limited Tender Enquiries, late bids received after the specified date and time must not be considered under any circumstances.
✅ Correct Action
The bid must be rejected immediately — no exceptions, no discretion, regardless of the reason given by the supplier.
🚫 There is NO provision to accept a late bid in an ATE or LTE — even if the reason appears genuine.
entry.exam_insight:
🔥 High-Probability Exam Questions — Most Asked Facts
Fact / Common Trap ✅ Correct Answer
🔥 No GTE (Global Tender Enquiry) is permitted for procurements up to ₹200 Crores (Rule 161)
🔁 "Bid Security is automatically adjusted against Performance Security after award" FALSE. Bid Security is refunded only after receipt of Performance Security — not automatically adjusted unless specifically stated.
⚠️ Minimum time for bid submission in an Advertised Tender (domestic) 3 weeks (increases to 4 weeks if bids from abroad are sought)
📌 A firm quoting NIL charges — how must the bid be treated? Bid must be treated as UNRESPONSIVE and must not be considered.
📌 Annual Procurement Plans must be projected on GeM within 30 days of Budget approval
📌 Bid securities of unsuccessful bidders must be returned latest by The 30th day after contract award
🧠 Key Distinctions — Compulsory for Exam
Concept A vs. Concept B
Advertised Tender Enquiry
Used for procurement of ₹50 Lakhs and above.
Requires wide publication on CPPP. Minimum 3 weeks for submission.
Open to all eligible bidders. 		vs. Limited Tender Enquiry
Used for procurements up to ₹50 Lakhs.
Directly sent to more than 3 eligible suppliers.
No open publication required.
Bid Security (Earnest Money)
2–5% of estimated value.
Valid for 45 days beyond bid validity.
Ensures bidder honours their quote. Refunded AFTER Performance Security is received. 		vs. Performance Security
3–5% of contract value.
Valid for 60 days beyond all obligations + warranty.
Ensures successful bidder fulfills the actual contract.

Library books excluded from definition of
"Goods" under GFR Rule 143
Annual Procurement Plans on GeM within
30 days of Budget approval
Bid securities of unsuccessful bidders returned by
30th day after contract award
LPC handles purchases from ₹50,000 up to
₹5,00,000
Old items can be traded in when buying new under
Buy-Back Offer rule
Electrical appliances must carry BEE Star Rating of
Notified threshold or higher
Min. suppliers for Limited Tender Enquiry
More than 3 firms
GTE prohibited for procurements up to
₹200 Crores (Rule 161)

entry.title: General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017 — Chapter 2 & 6: Procurement, Losses & Financial Propriety
entry.official_text:
📜
Ministry of Finance · Government of India
Constitutional Basis — Government & Public Accounts
Art. 150 & 283(1)
Government Account: All moneys received by or on behalf of the Government — whether as dues, for deposit, remittance or otherwise — shall be brought into Government Account without delay.
Art. 284
Public Account: All moneys received by or deposited with any officer, other than revenues or public moneys raised by Government, shall be paid into the Public Account. This includes all moneys received by or deposited with the Supreme Court of India or any other Court (other than a High Court) within a Union Territory.
⚖️
Rule 21 · GFR 2017
Standards of Financial Propriety

Every officer incurring or authorizing expenditure from public moneys must be guided by high standards of financial propriety. The expenditure should not be prima-facie more than the occasion demands.

💡 The officer must ensure that government funds are spent wisely, prudently, and only to the extent necessary.
📦 Definition of Goods — Rule 143
✅ INCLUDES ❌ EXCLUDES
All tangible or intangible products such as:
• Software, technology transfer
• Licenses, patents & intellectual properties
• Works and services
• Transportation, insurance
• Installation, commissioning
• Training and maintenance 		Books, publications, periodicals, etc. procured for a library are strictly excluded from the definition of Goods under GFR.
🤝 Consulting vs. Non-Consulting Services — Rules 177 & 197
Rule 177 — CONSULTING SERVICE Rule 197 — NON-CONSULTING SERVICE
Any subject matter of procurement other than goods or works, involving:
• Professional, intellectual services
• Training & advisory services

NOTE: Does NOT include direct engagement of a retired Government servant. 		Procurement involving physical, measurable deliverables where performance standards can be clearly identified. Includes:
• Maintenance contracts
• Hiring of vehicles
• Building facilities management
• Security services
entry.guru_explanation:
🚫 The Golden Rule of Splitting — Anti-Fragmentation Principle

A demand for goods shall NOT be divided into small quantities to make piecemeal purchases. This rule prevents officers from intentionally:

❌ Bypassing GeM reverse auction rules by keeping value under the ₹10L threshold
❌ Avoiding seeking approval from higher authorities by splitting one big purchase into many small ones
🚨 Handling Losses & Defalcations — Rule 33
Situation Action Required
Any loss of public money, stamps, or government property Report immediately to the next higher authority
Petty losses of value up to ₹10,000 ❌ No need to report
Mistakes in assessments ❌ No need to report
Loss exceeding ₹50,000 due to fire, theft, or fraud 🚔 Police must be brought in for investigation
⏳ The Lifespan of a Sanction — Lapse Rule
Sanction Issued
Day 0
→
Payment Window
12 Months
→
If No Payment Made
SANCTION LAPSES

Key Point: If no payment (even in part) is made within 12 months from the date of issue of the sanction, it automatically lapses. Fresh sanction must be obtained.

📊 QCBS Grading System — Quality & Cost Based Selection
Grade Score Range Technical Marks Awarded
⭐ Outstanding 91 – 100 100
✨ Excellent 81 – 90 90
💎 Very Good 71 – 80 80
👍 Good 61 – 70 70
🔵 Very Fair 51 – 60 60
📋 Fair 41 – 50 50
📉 Average 31 – 40 40
⬇️ Below Average — Zero (0)
💀 Very Poor — 0
⚠️ Key Rule: Technical weightage in QCBS must never exceed 80%. Default ratio is 70:30 (Technical : Financial).
🧮 CTFS Calculation — Combined Technical & Financial Score (Weightage 70:30)
Bidder Formula Applied (70:30) CTFS Score Rank
Bidder 1 100×(70/100) + 76.92×(30/100) 93.07 🥇 L1
Bidder 2 90×(70/100) + 83.33×(30/100) 87.99 🥈 L2
Bidder 4 80×(70/100) + 100×(30/100) 86.00 🥉 L3
💰 Critical Financial Limits — GeM & Procurement Thresholds (Revised 2024)
Category / Method Financial Limit / Value
🛒 GeM PROCUREMENT
Direct GeM Purchase Up to ₹50,000 (Revised from ₹25,000 w.e.f 10.07.2024)
GeM L-1 (Lowest of 3 sellers) ₹50,000 to ₹10,00,000 (Revised w.e.f 10.07.2024)
GeM Online Bidding / Reverse Auction Above ₹10,00,000 (Revised from ₹5L w.e.f 10.07.2024)
📋 TENDER ENQUIRY
Purchase without Quotation Up to ₹50,000 on each occasion
Local Purchase Committee (LPC) ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 (Revised w.e.f 10.07.2024)
Limited Tender Enquiry Up to ₹50 Lakhs (Revised from ₹25L w.e.f 10.07.2024)
Advertised Tender Enquiry ₹50 Lakhs and above
🔐 SECURITY & ADVANCE PAYMENT
Bid Security (Earnest Money) 2% to 5% of estimated value
Performance Security 3% to 5% of contract value (Revised w.e.f 01.01.2024)
Advance Payment — Private Firms Max 30% of contract value
Advance Payment — Govt/PSU Max 40% of contract value
🏦 Facilities, Conditions & Eligibility
📅 Supplier Registration
Registered for a fixed period of 1 to 3 years. Must apply afresh for renewal after expiry.
⏰ Performance Security Validity
Must remain valid for 60 days beyond the date of completion of all contractual obligations including warranty.
🚫 Debarment Rules
Guilty under Prevention of Corruption Act: Debarred up to 3 years.
Breaching Code of Integrity: Debarred up to 2 years.
✅ Bid Security Exemptions
MSMEs, GeM Registered Bidders, Bidders with >₹500 Cr turnover (once in 3 FYs), GeM Vendor Assessed, Startups, BIS Certified primary product suppliers.
🔟 Step-by-Step: Two-Stage Bidding Process — Rule 164
  1. Stage 1 — Invitation: The Ministry/Department invites bids through an advertised tender containing technical aspects and terms without asking for a bid price.
  2. Stage 1 — Evaluation: An appropriate committee evaluates all eligible first-stage bids on technical merit.
  3. Stage 2 — Final Bids: The procuring entity invites all non-rejected bidders to present a final bid with bid prices in response to a revised set of terms and conditions.
🔟 Step-by-Step: Reporting of Losses — Rule 33
  1. Initial Report: Submit as soon as a suspicion arises that a loss has taken place — don't wait for confirmation.
  2. Investigation: Conduct a full and thorough enquiry into the circumstances of the loss.
  3. Final Report: Send to authorities indicating the nature of loss, rule violations, and prospects of recovery.
  4. Forwarding: Send a copy of the report to the Audit Officer and the Pay and Accounts Officer.
entry.practical_example:
📌
Scenario 1 · GeM Direct Purchase
Sr. Postmaster, Tiruchirappalli HO — Office Stationery ₹35,000
📋 Situation
Sr. Postmaster needs to procure office stationery worth ₹35,000 for day-to-day use.
🔍 Analysis
₹35,000 falls within the Direct GeM Purchase limit of up to ₹50,000 (revised w.e.f 10.07.2024).
✅ Action
Procurement can be made through any available supplier on GeM meeting the required quality and specifications — no bidding needed.
🌊
Scenario 2 · Loss Reporting (Rule 33)
Flood Damage to Postal Properties — Loss of ₹75,000
📋 Situation
A severe flood damages postal properties in the division — estimated loss of ₹75,000 to building communications (immovable property).
🔍 Analysis
Loss of immovable property exceeds ₹50,000. Although it's flood damage, reporting to higher authorities is mandatory.
✅ Action
Must be reported at once by the subordinate authority to the Government through the usual channel.
💻
Scenario 3 · Consulting Service Procurement
Department Hires Consultant for Logistics Algorithm — ₹40 Lakhs
📋 Situation
Department wishes to hire a consultant to design a new logistics algorithm, estimated to cost ₹40 Lakhs.
🔍 Analysis
₹40 Lakhs is less than ₹50 Lakhs — the threshold for publishing Expression of Interest (EOI) on CPPP.
✅ Action
Department can prepare a long list of potential consultants via formal/informal enquiries. No need to publish EOI on CPPP.

entry.title: Proprietary Article Certificate — GFR 2017
entry.official_text:
Rule 166 — Procurement of goods of proprietary nature.

Purchase of goods of proprietary nature, the source of which is limited to only one supplier, can be made without inviting tenders. In such cases, the following certificate shall be recorded by the competent authority:

"I am personally satisfied that these goods/services purchased are of the requisite quality and specification and have been procured from a reliable supplier at a reasonable price."

Conditions for Proprietary Article Purchase:

  • The item must be of a proprietary nature — i.e., manufactured/supplied by only one firm.
  • The Purchase Officer must be satisfied about quality, specification, and price.
  • A Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) must be recorded.
  • No comparative quotations are required if PAC is recorded.
entry.guru_explanation:
Normally in government procurement, you must get at least 3 quotations and go through a tendering process. But what if something is available only from ONE company?

That's where the Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) comes in. It's the government's way of saying: "We know this is only available from one supplier, so we're buying directly — but the officer takes responsibility."

When Can You Use PAC?

  • Only ONE manufacturer/supplier makes this product (e.g., a specific spare part for a particular machine)
  • The purchasing officer is satisfied it's needed and priced fairly

The Certificate is Personal Responsibility

The key words in the certificate are "I am personally satisfied" — this places accountability on the officer signing it. If it's later found that alternatives were available, the officer is liable for irregular procurement.

What PAC is NOT

PAC cannot be used just because you prefer a particular brand. The absence of genuine competition must be established, not just preference.
entry.practical_example:
Scenario: A GPO needs to procure a specific software module that is compatible only with their existing CBS (Core Banking Solution) system, manufactured by a single vendor. The postmaster wants to buy it directly.

Correct Procedure:

  1. Obtain a certificate from the technical officer confirming the software is proprietary and no alternatives exist.
  2. The competent purchase authority records the PAC as per Rule 166 GFR 2017.
  3. Direct procurement from the vendor is made after satisfying about the price being reasonable (get a price quotation from vendor and compare with market if possible).
  4. The PAC is filed with the purchase order — available for audit inspection.

Wrong approach: Saying "we prefer this vendor" is NOT sufficient for PAC. There must be genuine technical necessity for single-source procurement.
entry.exam_insight:
Key Facts for GFR Questions:

  • GFR 2017 replaced: GFR 2005 (effective 7 March 2017)
  • PAC governed by: Rule 166, GFR 2017
  • When PAC is used: Proprietary/single-source items only
  • Tenders required: Not required when PAC is recorded
  • Responsibility: The officer who signs PAC takes personal responsibility
  • Certificate text keywords: "I am personally satisfied"

Frequent Exam Question: "In which of the following situations can goods be procured without tendering under GFR 2017?" — Options include urgent purchase, proprietary article, petty purchase (up to ₹25,000). All can qualify but PAC specifically covers proprietary articles under Rule 166.
